## [2026-10-12](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-12.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707>)

This study trains a small linear reward head on frozen vision-language features by contrasting web captions with perturbed captions, avoiding human preference labels for head training while using labeled data to select the layer. It shows that strong reward-benchmark accuracy need not produce good candidate selection, and that retraining on verifier-labeled policy outputs can improve deployment-specific selection even as its VL-RewardBench score falls.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-12T10:07:12Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Reward Modeling, Multimodal, Negative Sampling

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–3 test four Qwen3-VL sizes and GLM-4.1V-9B; Table 1 reports 72.4% VL-RewardBench accuracy for the 32B probe versus published GPT-4o's 65.8%. Section 3.4 tests one verifier-driven adaptation round. The actual October 12 new listing plus official schedule imply October 12 00:00 UTC announcement, not the October 8 submission timestamp.

**Limitations:** Layer selection uses labeled development data; benchmark rank is not general reward quality. CHAIR supplies both caption labels and evaluation, Best-of-N cells are single-seed, and matched-pair comparisons are not token-matched. The approximate 1/1000 training-compute claim excludes shared backbone forwards. Code release is promised but unverified.

## [2026-10-08](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-08.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Judging in Latent Space: Efficient Generative Reward Modeling via Semantics-Preserving Compression](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09788>)

LatentGRM trains a rubric-based preference judge to replace lengthy textual assessments with compact sequences of continuous states, using semantic boundaries to guide compression. It preserves broadly comparable preference accuracy while reducing judging time in the tested settings, with an optional offline decoder for inspecting compressed teacher evaluations.

**Published:** 2026-10-07 · **First seen:** 2026-10-08T10:03:53Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Reward Modeling, Latent Reasoning, Semantic Compression

**Public availability:** 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09788>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Matched Qwen3-4B/8B judges share 35,612 training records. The 8B model averages 69.0 versus 68.1 across eight domains and runs 6.11–6.95 times faster in four timed domains at vote@5 on eight GPUs. Original v1: 2026-10-07T10:05:06Z; verified October 8 new-submission batch.

**Limitations:** Timing excludes offline rubric generation and interpretation; accuracy gains vary by domain. Reconstruction tests teacher-derived trajectories and does not establish faithful explanations of autonomous judgments. Evidence is limited to one backbone family and pairwise judging, without downstream RL validation or a verified author implementation.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290>)

Direct Preference Optimization converts a regularized preference-learning objective into a direct loss on preferred and rejected responses, avoiding a separately trained reward model and online policy rollouts. It remains a useful foundational baseline for aligning model behavior from offline preference pairs with a comparatively simple training pipeline.

**Published:** 2023-05-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Preference Optimization, Alignment, DPO

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290>) · [Code](<https://github.com/eric-mitchell/direct-preference-optimization>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper derives the objective and evaluates sentiment control, summarization, and single-turn dialogue against reinforcement-learning and supervised baselines; an author reference implementation is available.

**Limitations:** Its preference-model assumptions and dependence on offline data matter; the original experiments do not establish universal superiority to online RL or robustness under distribution shift.
